environment: app-auth-staging, Clerk development, remote staging D1

examples.input: I want to prepare food for a future low-energy day. I have no microwave and prefer familiar food that needs no cooking. Use what I already own.
examples.title: Pick two no-cook favorites
examples.summary: Choose familiar food you already have that’s ready to eat without cooking or a microwave.
steps: Check what ready-to-eat food you already have at home.
Choose two familiar options you’d be happy to eat on a low-energy day.
Note each option and where you keep it in your usual note.
examples.doneWhen: Two familiar, no-cook options you already have are noted.
verified: A retained its own original food task

examples.input: I am often away from my desk. I want the contact number and booking details for a future routine appointment easy to find on my phone. This is preparation for later.
examples.title: Keep appointment details in your pocket
examples.summary: Save a future routine appointment contact on your phone so you can find it when you’re away from your desk.
steps: On your phone, open the official website of a clinic you use or might consider for a routine appointment.
Find its appointment number or booking page, opening hours, and any new-patient or payment details you need.
Save the details in your phone contacts or a note you can quickly find; flag anything to confirm with the clinic.
examples.doneWhen: One clinic’s appointment contact and any unanswered practical questions are saved on your phone.
verified: New concern overrides earlier food request

limitations: Two synthetic scenarios do not establish broad content quality or medical safety
No public content approval or public launch
Other failure and quota scenarios were mocked automated checks, not forced live provider failures
No physical-device, second-browser-engine or load tests
